summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DHCP server for the private network it shares with node2/node3 (10.50.50.0/24 via eth1, pool .100-.200), and configured node2/node3 (CentOS Stream 10) to obtain their private-network address via DHCP (NetworkManager ipv4.method=auto) instead of a static assignment. Implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (pre-provisioned control node). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart/recovery protocol on all 4 managed nodes.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS (eth0=platform net, eth1=private net shared with node2/node3), node2/node3=CentOS Stream 10 (enp1s0=platform, enp8s0=private, NetworkManager-managed), node4=Ubuntu control node with ansible-core + community.general + ansible.netcommon preinstalled

Established SSH access from node4 to node1 (as 'vyos' user, since root is locked) and to node2/node3 (as root) using the cluster ed25519 keypair; added the vyos user's key via VyOS's own persistent `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` config command

Wrote /root/ansible-dhcp/inventory.ini and playbook.yml on node4: play 1 (dhcp_server=node1) sets eth1 to 10.50.50.254/24 and configures a Kea-backed VyOS DHCP server (shared-network PRIVATE-LAN, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, subnet-id 1, pool 10.50.50.100-200, default-router/name-server options, lease 3600s) via configure/commit/save; play 2 (dhcp_clients=node2,node3) uses community.general.nmcli to set ipv4.method=auto on the enp8s0 'Wired connection 2' profile, reactivates it, and waits for/reports the leased address

Debugged two VyOS-specific issues found live: `set -e` combined with sourcing VyOS's script-template silently aborts the script (removed it); this VyOS rolling release's DHCP schema no longer supports subnet-parameters/default-router/name-server directly under subnet (requires subnet-id and nested 'option' node) - fixed playbook syntax to match by inspecting the live config templates

Ran the playbook to completion: node1 changed (DHCP server + interface configured), node2 leased 10.50.50.101, node3 leased 10.50.50.100 from node1's DHCP server; confirmed active Kea leases on node1 matching client addresses
Verified idempotency by re-running the playbook (node1 task reports changed=0 on second run)

Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id, uptime, live DHCP leases/addresses) on all 4 nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native `reboot`, polling each until exec access returned, confirming a new boot_id each time, and verifying post-restart recovery (VyOS eth1 address and isc-kea-dhcp4-server persisted/active on node1; node2/node3 re-acquired their same DHCP leases and pinged node1's private IP; node4's ansible playbook directory persisted and a full playbook re-run afterward succeeded cluster-wide)

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DHCP server on private network shared with node2/node3
evidence.summary: Ansible play 'Apply VyOS interface address and DHCP server configuration' reports changed:[node1]; show dhcp server leases confirms two active leases (10.50.50.100 node3, 10.50.50.101 node2) served by node1's DHCP server on subnet PRIVATE-LAN

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 configured to obtain address via DHCP rather than static
evidence.summary: nmcli module ensured ipv4.method=auto on enp8s0's connection profile (no static ipv4.addresses); after reactivation node2 leased 10.50.50.101/24 and node3 leased 10.50.50.100/24, both dynamic via DHCP, matching prior baseline showing no static config on that interface

Playbook /root/ansible-dhcp/playbook.yml executed via ansible-playbook from node4 (control node) against inventory.ini covering node1 (dhcp_server group) and node2/node3 (dhcp_clients group); syntax-checked and run to completion, then re-run to confirm idempotency

evidence.requirement: node1 restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4098161f...; reboot triggered; post-restart boot_id 3b72fac4... (changed); eth1 address 10.50.50.254/24 persisted and isc-kea-dhcp4-server.service active running after reboot, confirming DHCP server recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8f258838...; reboot triggered; post-restart boot_id 3f1eca20... (changed); re-acquired same DHCP lease 10.50.50.101/24 via ipv4.method=auto and successfully pinged node1's private IP 10.50.50.254

evidence.requirement: node3 restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id be303eb3...; reboot triggered; post-restart boot_id 8cb7f467... (changed); re-acquired same DHCP lease 10.50.50.100/24 via ipv4.method=auto and successfully pinged node1's private IP 10.50.50.254

(changed); /root/ansible-dhcp/ playbook files persisted and a full ansible-playbook re-run afterward succeeded across node1/node2/node3, confirming the control node's tooling and cluster-wide configuration remained functional
